diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Combined with {\bf Theorem \ref{Global-Convergence}}-$ (i)$, we get
	\[
	\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left\|\nabla^{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathcal{P}} E^n\right\|_{\mathcal{P}_{\phi^n}}=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\left\|\nabla^{\mathcal{R}}_{\mathcal{P}} E(\phi_g)\right\|_{H^1}=0.
	\]

Since $\{E(\phi^n)\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is monotonic decreasing and bounded below (with $E(\phi^n)\le E(\phi^0)$), the sequence $\{\phi^n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is uniformly bounded in $H_0^1(\mathcal{D})$. Hence, there exists a subsequence $\{\phi^{n_j}\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ converging weakly in $H_0^1(\mathcal{D})$ to some $\phi_g\in\mathcal{M}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition Property-P (iii) provides a local Lipschitz estimate \|∇(φ)−∇(ψ)\|_{H¹} ≤ C_φ‖φ−ψ‖_{H¹}, which is a strong-to-strong continuity statement requiring ‖φ^{n_j}−φ_g‖_{H¹}→0. However, the proof only establishes weak convergence φ^{n_j}⇀φ_g in H¹ (from uniform boundedness and reflexivity). Weak convergence does not imply strong H¹ convergence, so the Lipschitz estimate cannot be applied to conclude that ∇_P^R E(φ^{n_j}) converges weakly to ∇_P^R E(φ_g). The subsequent step—passing from ‖∇_P^R E^n‖_{P_{φ^n}}→0 to ‖∇_P^R E(φ_g)‖_{H¹}=0—therefore lacks justification. A valid argument would require a separate compactness step: using the strong L² convergence (Rellich–Kondrachov) together with the specific structure H_φφ = H_0φ + (f(ρ_φ)−ΩL_z)φ to show that H_{φ^{n_j}}φ^{n_j}−λ_{φ^{n_j}}φ^{n_j}→0 in H^{-1}, which combined with the uniform coercivity of P_{φ^{n_j}} yields the critical-point condition at φ_g. This non-trivial limit-passing argument is absent from the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unjustified citation of Property-P (iii) with a direct compactness argument: (1) use the strong L² convergence of φ^{n_j}→φ_g (Rellich–Kondrachov) and the polynomial growth of f to show the nonlinear term (f(ρ_{φ^{n_j}})−ΩL_z)φ^{n_j}→(f(ρ_{φ_g})−ΩL_z)φ_g in L²; (2) combine with the linear term H_0φ^{n_j}⇀H_0φ_g in H^{-1} to get H_{φ^{n_j}}φ^{n_j}→H_{φ_g}φ_g in H^{-1}; (3) use ‖∇_P^R E(φ^{n_j})‖_{H¹}→0 (from the P-norm descent and uniform norm equivalence) to conclude H_{φ_g}φ_g−λ_gφ_g=0 in H^{-1}, i.e., φ_g is a critical point. Then invoke weak lower semicontinuity of E in H¹ together with the energy convergence E(φ^{n_j})→E_g to conclude E(φ_g)=E_g.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem Global-Convergence (part ii) does not establish that every weak limit point of the iteration is a critical point of E, which is the key step needed to conclude that the limit is a minimizer. All downstream results (Local-Convergence, Var-P-convergence, Corollary E-eq-Phi) rely on the local convergence theory and are independent of this global proof gap, but the stated global convergence guarantee (that the iteration converges to a minimizer) is not fully supported by the written proof.
issues.title: Invalid inference from local Lipschitz continuity to weak gradient convergence in global convergence proof
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained, standard compactness argument (strong L² convergence + structure of H_φ + weak lower semicontinuity of E) that adds a few lines to the proof without altering any statement, changing the proof architecture, or weakening any conclusion. The theorem remains fully valid; only the written justification for one inference step is incomplete. This fits the moderate criterion: a non-trivial but local argument is missing, yet no global reconstruction or loss of content is required.
